source: Shem Tov Hebrew Matthew (Even Bochan, Ibn Shaprut c. 1385; critical text ed. G. Howard, base ms British Library Add. 26964)

verses.translation: After{H310} this{H2088} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}: The kingdom{H4438} of heaven{H8064} is like{H1819} a singular{H3173} man{H120}, master{H113} of his house{H1004}, who hires{H7936} in the morning{H1242} to hire{H7936} laborers{H6466}.

one_way_hebrew: מלכות שמים דומה ל... — the native rabbinic parable formula (מָשָׁל, למה הדבר דומה); the whole opening is stock Hebrew parable-language, not translation-Greek.
שכר (H7936) — the Torah's hiring verb (Deut 24:14-15), which governs this parable: the law of the hired laborer's same-day wage is the statute the householder keeps in v. 8.
greek_deviations: The base text reads המשכיר ('who hires'), where mss ABCDEFG read המשכים ('who rose early'), matching Greek ἅμα πρωΐ ('early in the morning'). The base also lacks 'for his vineyard' — ABDEFG add לכרמו after פועלים.
translation_notes: אדם יחיד אדון ביתו — 'a singular man, the master of his house,' for Greek ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδεσπότῃ ('a man, a householder'); the Hebrew splits the compound into native idiom.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק פ״ד (Perek 84) begins here.
The circulating transcription prints אחרזה as one word; Howard's text reads אחר זה, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (20:1): המשכיר] המשכים ABCDEFG; פועלים] + לכרמו ABDEFG.

verses.translation: And he hired{H7936} them for one{H259} dinar for the day{H3117}, and sent{H7971} them to his vineyard{H3754}.

translation_notes: דינר — the Roman denarius in its rabbinic-Hebrew dress (dinar), the Mishnah's everyday coin word; no biblical Strong's number exists for it.

verses.translation: And he went out{H3318} in the third{H7992} hour of the day{H3117} and saw{H7200} others{H312} standing{H5975} idle{H988} in the market{H7784}.

one_way_hebrew: בטלים (H988, batel) — Ecclesiastes' word for ceasing from labor (Eccl 12:3, וּבָטְלוּ הַטֹּחֲנוֹת); שוק (H7784) — the street of Prov 7:8 and Eccl 12:4-5. The verse is built from the vocabulary of Hebrew wisdom literature.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (20:3): ויצא] ויבא EF; בשוק בטלים] transposed (בטלים בשוק) ABCDEFG.

verses.translation: And he said{H559} to them: Go{H1980}, you{H859} also{H1571}, to my vineyard{H3754}, and what is fitting I will give{H5414} you.

translation_notes: ראוי ('fitting, due') — a post-biblical Hebrew word with no Strong's number; the register of the text is living medieval Hebrew, not archaizing back-translation.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (20:4): ובראוי] והראוי ABDEFG.

verses.translation: And they went{H1980}. And he went out{H3318} again{H5750} at noon{H6672} and also at the ninth{H8671} hour{H8160}, and did{H6213} so{H3651}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (20:5): ויצאו] ויצא ABDEFG; בשעה] בשעת A; תשיעית] התשיעית ABDEF.

verses.translation: And at the eleventh{H259}{H6240} hour{H8160} he went out{H3318} likewise, and found{H4672} others{H312} standing{H5975}, and said{H559} to them: Why{H4069} are you standing{H5975} idle{H988} all{H3605} the day{H3117}?

translation_notes: ג״כ — the ms abbreviates גם כן ('likewise') with scribal gershayim, as a Hebrew copyist writes for Hebrew readers.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (20:6): ובאחת] ובשנים A; שעה] שעות EF, omit D.

verses.translation: And they answered{H6030} him that no man{H120} had hired{H7936} us. And he said{H559} to them: Go{H1980}, you{H859} also{H1571}, to my vineyard{H3754}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (20:7): לכו] omit G; אליהם] להם AG.

verses.translation: And it came to pass{H1961} at the time{H6256} of evening{H6153}, the owner{H1167} of the vineyard{H3754} said{H559} to the one set{H5324} over{H5921} the laborers{H6466}: Call{H7121} them, that I may give{H5414} them their wages{H7939}. And he began{H2490} with the last{H314} and finished{H3615} with the first{H7223}.

one_way_hebrew: לעת ערב... ואתן להם שכרם — the householder keeps the Torah's wage law to the letter: 'at his day thou shalt give him his hire, neither shall the sun go down upon it' (Deut 24:15; Lev 19:13, 'the wages of him that is hired shall not abide with thee all night'). The parable's evening payment is a Torah-observance the Greek reader cannot see; שכר (H7939) is the statute's own word.
לעת ערב — the exact phrase of Gen 8:11 (לעת ערב) and Isa 17:14.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (20:8): לניצב] omitted variants not recorded; the verse is stable across the mss.

verses.translation: And the last{H314} ones received{H6901} one{H259} dinar.

one_way_hebrew: קבלו (H6901, qabal) — the late-biblical receiving verb (Esth 4:4; 9:23; Ezra 8:30), exactly the register a 1st-century Hebrew author writes; classical Hebrew would use לקח.

verses.translation: And the first{H7223} ones thought{H2803} to take{H3947} more{H3148}, but he gave{H5414} to all{H3605} of them only a dinar.

one_way_hebrew: יותר (H3148) — Ecclesiastes' word for 'more, surplus' (Eccl 2:15; 6:8,11; 7:11), again the late-Hebrew wisdom register.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads יורת; Howard's text reads יותר, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (20:10): G omits והוא... דינר; ABDEF read נתן לכל אחד דינר ('he gave to each one a dinar'); חשבו] והחושבים DG; והראשונים] G omits.

verses.translation: And the first{H7223} ones murmured{H3885} against{H5921} the owner{H1167} of the vineyard{H3754},

one_way_hebrew: וילונו (H3885, lun) — the wilderness-murmuring verb: 'the whole congregation murmured (וילונו) against Moses and Aaron' (Exod 16:2; Num 14:2; 16:11 'against YHWH'). The laborers replay Israel's murmuring against the master who feeds them; Greek ἐγόγγυζον translates this very idiom (LXX of Exod 16).

verses.translation: saying{H559}: These{H428} last{H314} ones toiled{H5998} one{H259} hour{H8160}, and you made them equal{H7737} with{H5973} us who toiled{H5998} all{H3605} the day{H3117} and the heat{H2721}!

one_way_hebrew: חורב (H2721) — the day-laborer's complaint in Jacob's own words: 'in the day the heat (חרב) consumed me, and the frost by night' (Gen 31:40). Greek καύσων translates; the Hebrew laborer complains in the vocabulary of Scripture's archetypal underpaid worker.
עמל (H5998) — Ecclesiastes' toil-verb (Eccl 2:11,21; 5:15).
textual_notes: The circulating transcription omits אותם; Howard's text reads והשוית אותם עמנו, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (20:12): והשוית] והשויתה A.

verses.translation: And he answered{H6030} one{H259} of them and said{H559} to him: My beloved{H157}, I do{H6213} you no injustice{H5766}. Did I not hire{H7936} you for one{H259} dinar?

one_way_hebrew: עול (H5766) — the Torah's word for injustice in judgment and in measures (Lev 19:15,35, לא תעשו עול); the master denies wrongdoing in the statute's own terms. Greek οὐκ ἀδικῶ σε translates it.
אהובי ('my beloved', H157) — where Greek has ἑταῖρε ('comrade'); the Hebrew master speaks covenant affection, not Greek politeness.
translation_notes: א״ — the ms writes the numeral אחד ('one') by abbreviation with gershayim, a native Hebrew scribal habit.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (20:13): לאחד מהם] להם A; לו] omit G; א״] omit G.

verses.translation: Take{H3947} it and go{H1980}. If I want{H7521} to give{H5414} to this{H2088} last{H314} one as to you{H3644} —

textual_notes: The sentence runs over the verse-break into v. 15, exactly as vv. 32-33 of chapter 24 do — the Hebrew text is a continuous discourse over which the verse numbers were later laid.

verses.translation: shall I not do{H6213} according to my will{H7522}? Is your eye{H5869} evil because{H834} I am good{H2896}?

one_way_hebrew: The evil-eye idiom is Torah Hebrew: 'beware... and thine eye be evil (ורעה עינך) against thy poor brother' (Deut 15:9; cf. Prov 23:6, רע עין) — the grudging eye of the man who resents another's getting. Greek ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου πονηρός is a word-for-word calque of this Hebrew idiom; in Greek it explains nothing, in Hebrew it is a statute's phrase.
translation_notes: הידע — the printed text has הידע ('does it know'), a ד/ר confusion for הירע ('is it evil'), which mss ABDG read (EF: הרע) and the idiom requires; Howard's English follows the variant ('is your eye evil'). The translation follows the sense.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (20:15): הידע] הירע ABDG, הרע EF.

verses.translation: So{H3651} the last{H314} will be first{H7223}, and the first{H7223} last{H314}. Many{H7227} are the called{H7121}, and few{H4592} the chosen{H977}.

one_way_hebrew: קרואים/נבחרים — 'called' (H7121) and 'chosen' (H977): the pair of Israel's own vocation-words (Isa 48:12, 'my called'; Deut 7:6-7, the election verb בחר). The saying recurs at 22:14.
greek_deviations: The closing sentence 'many are the called, and few the chosen' stands here in the Hebrew as in the Byzantine Greek and KJV of 20:16; the modern critical Greek text omits it at this verse (keeping it only at 22:14). Shem Tov sides with the fuller reading.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (20:16): יהיה] יהיו AB.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} drew near{H7126} to Yerushalayim{H3389}, and took{H3947} his twelve disciples{H8527} in secret{H5643} and said{H559} to them:

translation_notes: י״ב — the numeral 12 by Hebrew letter-abbreviation; ירושלם — the ms spells Jerusalem defectively, as the Tanakh itself does (the transcriber's footnote notes the 'biblical spelling').
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק פ״ה (Perek 85) begins here.

verses.translation: Behold{H2009}, we are going up{H5927} to Yerushalayim{H3389}, and the Son{H1121} of Man{H120} will be delivered{H4560} to the chiefs{H1419} of the sages{H2450} and the priests{H3548}, and they will condemn{H2325} him to death{H4191}.

one_way_hebrew: עולים לירושלם — 'going UP to Yerushalayim': the Hebrew pilgrim idiom (עלה, H5927; Ps 122:4, 'whither the tribes go up'). Greek ἀναβαίνομεν preserves the direction because it translates this idiom.
וייחייבוהו (from חוב/חייב) — the rabbinic court verb for declaring one liable (חייב מיתה, 'liable to death,' m.Sanhedrin passim). The sentence is framed in Hebrew legal language.
greek_deviations: The Hebrew names the judges 'the chiefs of the SAGES and the priests' (גדולי החכמים והכהנים) — the sages (chakhamim), the rabbinic authorities, stand where Greek has 'the chief priests and scribes.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (20:18): לירושלם] אל ירושלם A; האדם] אדם A; החכמים והכהנים] transposed A; וייחייבוהו] ויחייבוהו ABCDG, ויחריבוהו EF; למות] למיתה A.

verses.translation: And they will also deliver{H4560} him to the Gentiles{H1471} to strike{H5221} him and to put an end{H7673} to him — and on the third{H7992} day{H3117}...
words: and to put an end to him

one_way_hebrew: ולהשביתו (H7673, shavat) — 'to make him cease': the verb of Dan 9:27 (ישבית) and of God's own resting; used of a person it means to bring him to a full stop. The Hebrew has no crucifixion word here at all.
greek_deviations: No cross and no explicit resurrection verb: Greek Matthew reads 'to mock, and to scourge, and to crucify him; and the third day he shall rise again.' The base Hebrew text reads 'to strike him and to put an end to him, and on the third day —' breaking off. Mss BDEFG complete it with יקום ('he will rise'); ms A reads ולתלותו ולהלקותו ('to hang him and to flog him'), assimilating toward the Greek.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (20:19): ולהשביתו] ולתלותו ולהלקותו A, ולהלקותו BDEFG; השלישי] + יקום BDEFG ('he will rise'); וגם ימסרו] וימסרו A.

The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads 'to lift him up with warp and woof' (a medieval Hebrew circumlocution for a cross) 'but he will stand up alive on the third day' — showing how a related Hebrew text filled the same gap.

verses.translation: Then{H227} the wife{H802} of Zavdiel came{H935} with{H5973} her sons{H1121}, bowing down{H7812} and requesting{H1245} a request{H1246} from him.

one_way_hebrew: מבקשת בקשה (H1245, H1246) — the cognate-accusative 'requesting a request' is Esther's court idiom exactly (Esth 5:6-7, שאלתי ובקשתי; 7:2-3): a petitioner before a king. Greek αἰτοῦσά τι ('asking something') flattens the Hebrew figure.
translation_notes: זבדיאל — the ms Hebraizes Zebedee as Zavdiel ('El has endowed'), a genuine Hebrew name (Neh 11:14; 1 Chr 27:2); Greek Ζεβεδαίου is a transliteration of the Hebrew root זבד (Gen 30:20).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (20:20): בא] omit AG.

verses.translation: And he said{H559} to her: What{H4100} do you want{H7521}? And she said{H559}: That you command{H6680} that these{H428} my two{H8147} sons{H1121} sit{H3427} — the one{H259} at your right{H3225} and the second{H8145} at your left{H8040} — in your kingdom{H4438}.

one_way_hebrew: שתצוה — 'that you COMMAND' (H6680): the mother asks for a royal decree, the king's word that makes it so; Greek εἰπὲ ('say') is weaker than the Hebrew's צוה.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads ואמר; Howard's text reads ויאמר, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (20:21): ותאמר] ויאמר B; בני אלה] בניה אלה B, בניה DG; והשני] והאחד D.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} answered{H6030} them: You do not know{H3045} what{H4100} you are requesting{H1245}. Are you able{H3201} to bear{H5445} the sufferings and the death{H4194} that I am destined{H6264} to bear{H5445}? And they said{H559}: We are able{H3201}.

one_way_hebrew: לסבול (H5445, saval) — the Suffering Servant's own verb: 'surely he has carried our pains (סבלם)' (Isa 53:4), 'their iniquities he shall bear (יסבל)' (Isa 53:11). Twice in one verse the Hebrew puts the Servant's carrying-verb in Yeshua's mouth; Greek πίνειν ('drink') has moved to the cup metaphor and lost Isaiah.
יסורין — the rabbinic word for chastening-sufferings (from יסר, the root of Isa 53:5's מוסר, 'the chastisement of our peace was upon him'); no Greek word carries this freight.
greek_deviations: The question is asked plainly — 'Can you bear the sufferings and the death that I am destined to bear?' — where Greek Matthew veils it in the cup figure ('Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of?'). The Hebrew names the thing; the cup then appears in v. 23 as its seal.
translation_notes: מיתה — the rabbinic-Hebrew form for 'death (as undergone)' (מיתת בית דין); tagged H4194 by root.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads היסוריו; Howard's text reads היסורין, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (20:22): תדעון] תדעו A; התוכל] התוכלון ABDEF, התוכלו G; היסורין] ביסורים C; עתיד] omit G.

verses.translation: And he said{H559} to them: Drink{H8354} my cup{H3563}; but to seat{H3427} you at my left{H8040} or even at my right{H3225} is not mine to give{H5414}, except to him who is prepared{H3559} before{H6440} my Father{H1}.

one_way_hebrew: כוס (H3563) — the prophets' cup of destiny (Ps 16:5; Isa 51:17; Jer 25:15); נכון לפני (H3559) — 'established/prepared before,' the idiom of 1 Kgs 2:45 (כסא דוד יהיה נכון לפני יהוה, 'the throne of David shall be established before YHWH') — the very question at issue: who sits enthroned beside the king.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (20:23): שתו] שתבאו EF; והושיבו] ותושיבו EF; לשמאלי...לימיני] transposed EF; גם] omit ABDEFG; לפני] בעיני EF.

verses.translation: And the ten{H6235} heard{H8085}, and it burned{H2734} in their eyes{H5869} in the matter{H6045} of the two{H8147} brothers{H251}.

one_way_hebrew: ויחר בעיניהם — the anger idiom of Gen 31:35 and 45:5 (חרה + the personal seat of the feeling); Greek ἠγανάκτησαν is one flat verb. ענין (H6045) is Ecclesiastes' word for a 'matter, business' (Eccl 1:13; 3:10).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (20:24): בעיניהם בעניין] בעינם מענין ABDG, מענין EF; אחים] האחים A.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} brought them near{H7126} to himself and said{H559} to them: Know{H3045} that the princes{H5387} of the Gentiles{H1471} have dominion{H7287} over them, and their great{H1419} ones seek{H1245} their souls{H5315}.

one_way_hebrew: רודים (H7287, radah) — the Torah's dominion verb, and the very one Israel is forbidden to use on a brother: 'thou shalt not rule (תרדה) over him with rigour' (Lev 25:43,46,53). The saying that follows ('it shall not be so among you') is Lev 25 applied: Gentile princes do radah; brothers do not.
נשיאי (H5387) — the Torah's own word for chiefs (Num 1:16).
translation_notes: מבקשים לנפשם — either 'seek their lives' (the idiom בקש נפש, 1 Kgs 19:10) or 'seek for themselves'; mss ABEF read לכבשם ('to subdue them', H3533), which Howard's English follows: 'seek (to subdue them).'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (20:25): ויקרבם] ויקריבם A; לנפשם] לכבשם ABEF.

verses.translation: It will not be so{H3651} among{H996} you; for he who wants{H7521} to be great{H1419} among you will serve{H8334} you,

one_way_hebrew: שרת (H8334) — the sanctuary-service verb (Exod 28:35, 'to minister in the holy place'; Num 3:6). Greatness among the disciples is defined by the priest's word for ministering before God; Greek διάκονος cannot carry the Temple echo.
translation_notes: ישקת — the printed text's ישקת is a scribal slip for ישרת ('will serve'), as mss ABEF read (D: ישית); the translation follows the sense, with the transcriber's footnote concurring.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (20:26): ישקת] ישרת ABEF, ישית D; ביניכם²] omit EF.

verses.translation: and he who wants{H7521} to be first{H7223} among{H996} you will be to you a servant{H5650} —

one_way_hebrew: The pair שרת (v. 26) / עבד (v. 27) is the Hebrew ladder of service: the minister (priestly word) and the bond-servant (עבד יהוה, Moses' own title, Deut 34:5). Greek διάκονος/δοῦλος translates the pair without its biblical resonance.

verses.translation: just as{H834} the Son{H1121} of Man{H120} came{H935} not that they should serve{H8334} him, but he himself to serve{H8334}, and to give{H5414} his soul{H5315} as a ransom{H3724} for many{H7227}.

one_way_hebrew: כופר (H3724) — the Torah's ransom word: 'they shall give every man a ransom for his soul (כפר נפשו)' (Exod 30:12); 'none can by any means redeem his brother... nor give to God a ransom for him (כפרו)' (Ps 49:8). The Hebrew sentence — לתת נפשו כופר — is built from Exod 30:12's own elements; Greek λύτρον translates the word but not the statute.

לרבים — 'for MANY': Isa 53:11-12's word (יצדיק צדיק עבדי לרבים... והוא חטא רבים נשא). Bearing (סבל, v. 22), soul-giving, and 'the many' — the Servant Song's three markers converge in the Hebrew of vv. 22-28.
translation_notes: ששר — a scribal slip for כאשר ('just as'), as mss ABDEFG read; the transcriber's footnote concurs, and the translation follows the sense.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (20:28): ששר] כאשר ABDEFG; אדם] האדם AD; הוא] omit ABCDEFG.

verses.translation: As they{H1992} were entering{H3664} Yericho{H3405}, one{H259} company{H2267} went{H1980} after{H310} him.

greek_deviations: ENTERING Yericho — Greek Matthew and Mark have the healing as they DEPARTED from Jericho (ἐκπορευομένων), Luke as he came NEAR to Jericho (Luke 18:35). The Hebrew Matthew stands with Luke's approach, against Greek Matthew — and the whole scene that follows (vv. 30-34) matches Luke 18:35-43 in detail.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק פ״ו (Perek 86) begins here.

verses.translation: And behold{H2009}, two{H8147} blind men{H5787} were coming out{H3318} beside{H681} the road{H1870}; and they heard{H8085} the sound{H6963} of the multitude{H1995} and asked{H7592} what{H4100} this was, and it was said{H559} to them: The prophet{H5030} Yeshua{H3442} from Nazareth is coming{H935}. Then{H227} they cried out{H6817}, saying{H559}: Son{H1121} of David{H1732}, have mercy on us{H2603}!

one_way_hebrew: חננו (H2603) — 'be gracious to us': the Psalter's blind-beggar cry (Ps 123:3, חננו יהוה חננו; Ps 6:3). The men pray a psalm; Greek ἐλέησον translates it.
וישמעו קול ההמון — 'they heard the sound of the multitude' (המון, H1995), the phrase of 1 Kgs 18:41 (קול המון הגשם) and Dan 10:6.
greek_deviations: The blind men's question and the crowd's answer — 'they asked what this was, and it was said to them: the prophet Yeshua from Nazareth is coming' — is Luke 18:36-37 verbatim in substance, and is entirely absent from Greek Matthew. The Hebrew Matthew carries Luke's fuller scene.
'The PROPHET Yeshua from Nazareth' — the crowd's title in Matt 21:11 (Greek) appears here on the road; the Hebrew text uses it a chapter early, consistently.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads בנ דוד חננן; Howard's text reads בן דוד חננו, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (20:30): וישאלוהו] וישאלו ABCDG, ויאמרו EF; ויאמר] ויאמרו ABDEF; the spelling of מנזא״רית varies across the mss (מנאזרת ACDG, מנזרת B).

verses.translation: And the company{H2267} rebuked{H1605} them, and even so they were crying out{H6817} and saying{H559}: Master{H113}, Son{H1121} of David{H1732}, have mercy on us{H2603}!

one_way_hebrew: גערו (H1605, ga'ar) — the rebuke that silences (Gen 37:10; Ps 106:9); the blind men out-cry it, as the stones would in Luke 19:40.
translation_notes: ואעפ״כ — the ms abbreviates ואף על פי כן ('and even so') with gershayim: a running Hebrew scribal shorthand, unintelligible except to Hebrew readers.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (20:31): the whole verse omitted in G; ואעפ״כ הם] לאמר הסו והם ABDEF ('saying: Hush! and they...'); ואומרים] ואמרו EF.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} stood still{H5975} and called{H7121} them, and said{H559}: What{H4100} do you want{H7521} to be done{H6213} for you?

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (20:32): no significant variants recorded.

verses.translation: And they said{H559}: Master{H113}, that our eyes{H5869} may be opened{H6491}.

one_way_hebrew: שתפקחנה עינינו — the blind men answer in Isaiah's own consonants: 'then the eyes of the blind shall be opened' (אז תפקחנה עיני עורים, Isa 35:5). פקח (H6491) is Scripture's dedicated verb for opening blind eyes, and Isa 35:5 is the messianic sign-text this healing enacts. Greek ἀνοιγῶσιν is a general 'open'; only the Hebrew quotes the prophecy.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} had compassion{H2550} on them and touched{H5060} their eyes{H5869}, and said{H559} to them: Your faith{H530} has healed{H7495} you. And immediately they saw{H7200}, and gave thanks{H3034} to El{H410} and went{H1980} after{H310} him; and all{H3605} the people{H5971} gave thanks{H3034} to El{H410} for this.

greek_deviations: 'They gave thanks to El... and all the people gave thanks to El for this' — Greek Matthew ends at 'they followed him.' The doxology is Luke 18:43 ('he followed him, glorifying God: and all the people, when they saw it, gave praise unto God') — a third Lukan agreement in this one pericope (vv. 29, 30, 34).

אמונתכם ריפא אתכם — 'your faith has healed you' stands in the Hebrew where Greek Matthew has only 'Jesus... touched their eyes and immediately they received sight'; the saying is Mark 10:52/Luke 18:42's.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads והודו לעל; Howard's text reads והודו לאל, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (20:34): ומיד] מיד F; לאל¹] האל A, ולא EF.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 20 in the Shem Tov Hebrew: (1) The vineyard parable turns on Torah wage-law — the master pays לעת ערב ('at evening time,' v. 8), obeying Deut 24:15/Lev 19:13 to the letter, and the laborers complain in Jacob's word for a day-laborer's misery (החורב, 'the heat,' Gen 31:40; v. 12); their murmuring is Israel's wilderness verb (וילונו, Exod 16:2; v. 11). (2) 20:16 keeps 'many are called and few are chosen' with the Byzantine/KJV text against the modern critical Greek. (3) 20:19 has no crucifixion word and no resurrection verb: 'to strike him and to put an end to him (ולהשביתו), and on the third day —'; mss BDEFG supply יקום ('he will rise'), ms A supplies hanging and flogging — the base text stands short of the Greek at the passion's sharpest point. (4) 20:22 asks 'Can you bear (לסבול) the sufferings and the death?' — the Suffering Servant's verb (Isa 53:4,11) — where Greek has the cup metaphor; v. 28 then gives 'his soul as a ransom (כופר, Exod 30:12; Ps 49:8) for MANY (לרבים, Isa 53:11-12).' (5) 20:25-27 ground the greatness-saying in Torah: Gentile princes 'have dominion' (רודים — Lev 25:43's forbidden verb), but among the disciples greatness is שרת, the priestly ministry-verb. (6) The Jericho healing (vv. 29-34) agrees with LUKE against Greek Matthew three times: they ENTER Jericho (v. 29 = Luke 18:35), the blind men ask and are told 'the prophet Yeshua from Nazareth is coming' (v. 30 = Luke 18:36-37, absent from Greek Matthew), and the scene closes with the double doxology to God (v. 34 = Luke 18:43). The blind men's request quotes Isa 35:5 in its own consonants (שתפקחנה עינינו, v. 33), and their cry חננו is the Psalter's (Ps 123:3). Shem Tov's section divisions fall at vv. 1 (Perek 84), 17 (85), and 29 (86).
